commits.subject: One game, one card: Soaked leads, Drop Zero becomes the classic build
commits.lede: /drop-zero boots water now, so its card was advertising a game nobody gets by default — 'build faster than they can shoot' when the guns are full of water. It becomes 'Drop Zero (classic)' at ?mode=classic, unfeatured and out of the nav: the same engine with ctx.mode flipped is one world, and a variant should stay reachable without competing for attention.

commits.subject: mobile-shot: check whether a page actually fits a phone
commits.lede: The desktop capture harness says nothing about whether a layout FITS. This opens a route in a real iPhone context — touch enabled, coarse pointer, correct DPR, which matters because without them you are testing a narrow desktop rather than a phone — screenshots the full page, and lists every element wider than the viewport with its tag, classes and text.

commits.subject: Re-stamp after the merge
commits.lede: The Vibe Times and the city-family worlds picked up commits while BLOB was being built, so their dates were a day stale the moment the branches came together.

commits.subject: Stamp BLOB, and repair the dates a shallow clone had flattened
commits.lede: `npm run stamp` gives the new world its date. It also corrects a dozen others: this checkout was shallow, so `git log -- <path>` for anything older than the clone boundary returned the boundary commit instead of nothing, and a previous run had written that one timestamp across every world whose code had not been touched recently. The script guards against a path resolving to *nothing*; it cannot tell that a path reso

commits.subject: BLOB: agar.io in the vibeverse — one dish, twenty-four rivals
commits.lede: A new world at /blob (and /agar, /agario, /cells, because that is what people type). You are a cell: everything smaller is food, everything bigger is a problem, and the only real decision is whether to spend half of yourself catching something that is running away.

commits.subject: Don't tell the paper where its own copy comes from
commits.lede: Issue №3 printed "the build log went missing for a week" in the weather column, twice, as though a quiet week were a fault. The brief was handing the model the *source* of the build record alongside the commits, and a rule saying not to mention the machinery did not stop it — a thing in the brief is a thing the writer will reach for.

commits.subject: 📰 The Vibe Times prints itself every morning, with a wire desk
commits.lede: The paper's masthead has claimed since July that it was written nightly. It wasn't: issue №1 shipped in July and sat on the front door into August, because writing it was a thing someone had to remember to do.

commits.subject: Give Soaked a source path git can actually resolve
commits.lede: `source` in the registry is passed straight to `git log -- <path>` by `npm run stamp`, so "src/royale (mode: water)" matched no path, produced no commits, and left Soaked as the one world on the grid with no "updated" date — and a failing freshness test on main.

commits.subject: Wallet: real balances in dollars, the spinning arc, and a test drop
commits.lede: Three things, and the first one was a real bug.

commits.subject: Water is the default now
commits.lede: /drop-zero opens SOAKED. It is the same 22 systems with ctx.mode flipped, and the water fight is the one worth playing — soakers, balloons, the glue gun, and last one dry wins. ?mode=classic is the way back to the bullets-and-health build for anyone who wants it, and /soaked stays a direct route.

commits.subject: SOAKED: the water-gun battle royale, wired up and playable
commits.lede: Eight systems behind ctx.mode === 'water', so one engine runs both games and classic stays byte-identical.

commits.subject: Wallet: hold more than one, and show what is actually in them
commits.lede: /wallet was a single card that said "payout address set" and then refused to say anything else. One address, no balances, no way to add a second — so somebody holding a MetaMask they have used for years AND a Base Account they made here last week could keep exactly one of them, and the app's only vocabulary for the other was "Create a Vibe Wallet". An invitation to make a third. The more wallets you had, the more ins

commits.subject: Arcade: a character shop with six originals you can buy and wear
commits.lede: The arcade had the loop that matters — pay, play, get paid — and one thing to spend on that you keep: hats. A hat is a good sink and a bad reason. Nobody opens a game to look at their hat; what people open a game to look at is who they are in it.

commits.subject: 📰 The front door opens with the paper instead of two buttons nobody pressed
commits.lede: "Start at the Terminal" and "The 3D hub" led `/game` — occupying the most valuable row on the page, pointing at two surfaces nobody uses. Both routes still exist and are still in the world list; they just no longer get the opening line.

commits.subject: 📜 Tap the date to see what changed — and fix the typecheck that was checking nothing
commits.lede: **First, the crash.** The wallet link I added to the Vibecoin chip referenced a `payout` variable I never declared. Tapping the chip white-screened the app with "payout is not defined". Fixed, and it reads the linked address when the panel opens rather than at mount, so linking a wallet and coming straight back shows the new state.

commits.subject: 🏝️ One plaza on Vibe Island, and a wallet you can actually find
commits.lede: **The layout.** Everything that costs or gives Vibecoin was scattered across a 110-unit island, and the character portal — one of the four things people actually use — sat at x = −34, sixty units and a jetpack ride from the shop it dresses you for. They now sit in one arc in the south-east:

commits.subject: 📬 The sign-in code autofills, and the box submits itself
commits.lede: Three things, and the first is the one that was actually asked for.

commits.subject: 🔐 The Vibe Wallet: a Base Account made with a passkey, and any wallet you own
commits.lede: Two doors now, for the two kinds of person who will open this card.

commits.subject: 🕰️ Re-stamp the worlds from a history deep enough to be true
commits.lede: `npm run stamp` reads each world's `source` out of the git log, and this repo is usually cloned shallow. The script guards the case where a path resolves to *nothing* — but not the case where it resolves to the clone's boundary commit, which is worse, because it looks like an answer. Twelve worlds were carrying 2026-07-21 for no reason other than that being as far back as the clone went.

commits.subject: 🏁 One Vibe Kart, and a lobby that starts the race for you
commits.lede: Two complaints, one shape. There were two Vibe Kart cards in the hub — `/kart` and `/kart-mp` — so the first decision a visitor made was one they could not yet have an opinion about, between two routes that render the same racetrack. And the multiplayer behind the second card was not really a lobby: it had a room code, a roster and a "Start race" button anybody could press, which works only if everyone is already sta

commits.subject: ✊ A table on the island: one hand against the house, provably fair
commits.lede: Walk up to the half-round table on the Vibe Island plaza, ante 25 ✦, and play one hand of rock-paper-scissors against the house. Smallest possible complete bet — no lobby, no opponent to find, ten seconds start to finish.

commits.subject: 🧭 Vibe Island leads, the running order moves to the top, and the map is current
commits.lede: **Ordering.** `ORDER` in `registry.ts` is the knob people reach for most, and it was seven hundred lines down, underneath every world entry. It is now the first thing in the file, with a comment saying that is what it is for. Vibe Island opens the collection — the gentlest door, works on a phone, the one to put in front of somebody who has never been here. Strange New Worlds moves to tenth. Orbit, the arcade and the

commits.subject: 🕰️ Every portal says when it last moved, and the wink finally gets used
commits.lede: Four of Jack's notes, and one thing found on the way.

commits.subject: 🛰️ ORBIT, invite links and a pot: the vibeverse gets something to bet on
commits.lede: The currency had places to spend it and no reason to want it. This is the reason: one shared sky, ten friends, one pot.

commits.subject: Air you can see through, and water on the worlds that have some
commits.lede: Two more of the things that separate a rendered frame from a diorama, and both turned out to be less about shading than about geometry.

commits.subject: One engine, two games: add the mode seam
commits.lede: ctx.mode is 'classic' (Drop Zero — bullets, health, a purple storm) or 'water' (SOAKED — soakers, dryness, the Downpour). One island, one set of 22 systems, and the difference is a lookup into mode/water.ts rather than a fork. Two battle royales would mean every bug fixed twice and every art pass done twice, and this project has already demonstrated how expensive one pass is.

commits.subject: The Odyssey gets a hull, and the planets get an atmosphere
commits.lede: The ship was a silhouette with blue stripes painted on it, which is fine at ninety units and is what you are looking at from nine. She now carries the `metal` bake at a 0.16-unit tile, sixty instanced greebles across the engineering hull, a lathed saucer at 96 segments, a deflector housing, a lit shuttlebay, seventy-six windows on two decks, a dorsal strobe, and running lights — port red, starboard green, the same co

commits.subject: People you can stand in front of, and columns that are not clip art
commits.lede: The characters were the weakest thing in the world and they were weak in the one place it costs most: three metres, face to face, which is where every conversation in this game happens. You walked up to a Vulcan master to ask her about Kolinahr and you were looking at a bowling pin.

commits.subject: A real renderer: HDR post, baked PBR surfacing, sky-probe IBL, ground scatter
commits.lede: The world shipped looking like coloured shapes on a coloured plane. Four things were missing and they turned out to be four specific things rather than a general lack of polish.

commits.subject: 🛍️ Vibecoin buys something you keep: cosmetics move onto the ledger
commits.lede: The arcade proved coins could be spent. It could not prove they were worth having, because everything you won there went straight back into the same machines — the currency had one sink and it was a loop.

commits.subject: 🖖 Strange New Worlds — twelve real Star Trek systems, and everyone on them talks back
commits.lede: /trek is the half of Star Trek where you shoot. This is the other half: make orbit somewhere nobody has been, run the sensors, then go down and ask it a question. No combat anywhere in it, on purpose.

commits.subject: Storm damage works; the beat was reading the wrong bar
commits.lede: Instrumenting dz:hit outside the zone showed a tick landing every simulated second, correctly sized — {amount: 0.504, shield: true} — with shield walking 100 -> 97.98 while health sat at exactly 100. skipToLive grants a full shield and applyDamage spends it first, like every other damage source, so the beat was watching a number that would not have moved for 200 seconds.

commits.subject: Floors and ramps were unbuildable on every street in every town
commits.lede: volumeClear() and isAnchored() contradicted each other about the ground. A wall's collider starts exactly on the lattice plane, but a floor's whole 0.25 m slab sits below it — the walking surface is the plane — and a ramp's staircase underhangs by half the wall thickness. Every POI has a solid apron whose top face IS that grid plane, so the very box isAnchored found as support was counted by volumeClear as an obstruc

commits.subject: Bot nameplates never compiled: one include, declared twice
commits.lede: three r160 prepends <colorspace_pars_fragment> to every non-raw ShaderMaterial, so PLATE_FRAG including it again declared LinearSRGBToLinearDisplayP3 twice and the whole fragment shader failed to compile — the nameplates over every bot rendered as nothing at all. This is the 'function already has a body' error the playtest surfaced during the harvest beat.

commits.subject: ⚡ GOD MODE — summon rain, snow and thunderstorms over the whole world
commits.lede: A chip next to the day/night switch opens a little palette: Clear, Rain, Snow, Storm. The day/night toggle is lobby-wide because everyone shares one sky; the weather is yours, because being the only person standing in a thunderstorm is funnier.

commits.subject: Loot: a held E can no longer be swallowed by the target it is waiting for
commits.lede: The interact edge was global: `prevInteract` latched true on every frame where nothing was in reach, so a press that began before the pickup arrived could never take it. Holding E while running onto a rifle — or while the gun you just knocked out of a chest settles — was silently refused until you let go and pressed again. The edge is now per-target (`takeArmed`), which is what the old rising edge was really trying t

commits.subject: dz-play: aim the build beats at ground the game will accept
commits.lede: build-place was never a builder bug. `aimPoint` puts the ghost at the full 10.5 m range when the look ray hits nothing, so clicking with the camera level in the middle of a POI asked for a wall inside somebody's concrete, `validate()` answered "blocked", and four correct refusals read as "nothing ever gets built". Instrumenting `collision.overlapBox` found the refusing box was a real slab genuinely intersecting the c

commits.subject: 🌆 Vibe City from the air: shadows, massing, rooftops, and a lighting grid
commits.lede: Pinch the camera out over Vibe City and what you saw was ninety extruded boxes standing on a painted plate. Nothing cast a shadow, so the towers appeared to hover a little above their own ground. Every roof was one flat colour — and roofs are most of what an aerial frame *is*, so the surface everybody looks at was the least-drawn thing in the scene. And one silhouette repeated at three heights, so the skyline had no

commits.subject: Loot: let a held interact sweep a pile, and name the containers
commits.lede: A floor item is a tap, but holding the key must still sweep a spill — walking into a chest's scatter with E down is how people actually collect loot. A quarter-second repeat in nearest-first order keeps that a sweep rather than a vacuum, so you can see what you took and let go before the fifth thing fills your last slot.

commits.subject: SOAKED foundations: multiplayer, the water rules, and a teammate who talks
commits.lede: Three pieces, none of which touch the single-player game that is already live.

commits.subject: Eleven levels, one per corner of the vibeverse
commits.lede: Ten new levels, and the interesting part is that they are different games rather than different paint.

commits.subject: 🦇 Four new code-built characters, and the heist stops nagging
commits.lede: THE CAST. Flux proved a character can be assembled from primitives and animated entirely from its own motion — no model file, no clips, no skating feet. That rig is now a design table, so a new character is an entry rather than a new animation system, and every one of them inherits the whole solver: stride that grows with speed, banking into turns, landing squash, breathing idle, blinks, and spring-driven secondary m

commits.subject: Shrink the zone before testing storm damage
commits.lede: The beat searched 48 bearings for dry ground outside the circle and found only sea, then reported a storm bug. Circle 1 has a 1250 m radius and the island's land radius is 1155 — there is no dry ground outside the first circle. That is a geometry fact, not a failure. Pull the safe zone in around the player first, then step out of it.

commits.subject: Measure the playtest in simulated seconds, not wall seconds
commits.lede: The first honest playtest called walk, jump, harvest and building broken. They were not. core.ts clamps dt to 1/15 and runs at most six fixed steps a frame, so at SwiftSHADER's fraction of a frame per second the simulation advances about 400x slower than the clock on the wall — the storm timer moved 0.05s in twenty. Holding W for four real seconds bought about a centimetre.

commits.subject: Take the pointer before playing: input is gated on it
commits.lede: player.controllable is false whenever ctx.input.locked is false, and input.locked is only ever set by the pointerlockchange handler. The one thing that calls requestPointerLock is the 'Drop in' button on the entry veil, which ?shot=1 deliberately does not render — so nothing ever asked for the pointer.

commits.subject: Move Drop Zero up the landing grid, and a harness that actually plays it
commits.lede: dz-shot proves the world renders; it says nothing about whether the game plays, because it poses a frozen player and takes a picture. Every system below the scenery — building, weapons, harvesting, loot, bots, the storm, the match phases — has never once been exercised. dz-play drives real input and asserts on the engine's own state after each beat, screenshots the failures, and keeps going so one broken system does

commits.subject: Card art for Drop Zero, from the running world
commits.lede: The plaza at Neon Heights, captured live at high quality with the match in its playing state — not key art, and not the spawn frame.

commits.subject: Stop the storm wall painting bolts across every ground frame
commits.lede: WALL_FRAG's streak term had no range falloff, and the vertical profile gated cover but not energy — so above the geometric top fade the wall stopped occluding while still emitting, and the additive surplus drew world-vertical bolts across the open sky. At zone 1 the wall is always on the horizon, so that was the sky of essentially every ground shot in the game.

commits.subject: Lift the shadows off black, and give the facades something to say
commits.lede: Shadowed ground was reading near-black with a heavy blue cast because the hemisphere fill was a two-point lerp between zenith and horizon — a 6:1-blue, green-deficient colour that no albedo could warm. It is now a cosine-weighted quadrature of the dome's own diffuse irradiance, plus an explicit warm bounce standing in for the sunlit walls a hemisphere light cannot see. The shadowed plaza goes from RGB 24.9,38.4,60.9

commits.subject: The ground was black because tinted() multiplies, and it was authored to replace
commits.lede: materials.tinted() multiplies its tint into an already-painted plate, in linear space. The district apron was asphalt (0.027 linear) times 0x4a4c50 (0.07) = 0.0019 albedo — darker than any real material. Every ground tint in pois.ts was written as if the tint replaced the base colour rather than compounding with it. Aprons, sidewalks, kerbs, crossings and markings now use documented near-white paving constants, and N

commits.subject: Race a hydroplane
commits.lede: Seafair is a boat race that grew an air show. The boats have been out on the lake since the first version of this world, running the real course at the real speed, and being unable to be one of them was the obvious hole in it.

commits.subject: Ground truth for captures, and a sky that is actually blue
commits.lede: match.fixed() held the phase machine at the title screen until ctx.input.locked. A headless capture never locks the pointer, so the phase stayed 'warmup' forever, the bus re-parked the player at 120 Hz, and match.jump() — which requires phase 'bus' — was a no-op. Every frame reviewed in this project has been a battle-bus frame. New match.skipToLive() and player.placeOnGround() make live ground state a first-class cal

commits.subject: 🪙 Vibecoin becomes a currency: a balance in every corner, and an arcade to spend it in
commits.lede: The ledger has worked for months and no visitor could tell. You could earn ninety coins on a floating island and the only evidence was a toast that faded in four seconds — there was nowhere in the app that said "this place has money in it, and you have some". And everything that touched the balance only ever paid *out*, so the number could only inflate. A number that only goes up is a score, not a currency.

commits.subject: Left turns left, and the crash hits like one
commits.lede: Two things.

commits.subject: Leaving the bus is a handshake, not a single call
commits.lede: match.jump() is a no-op until the phase machine actually reaches 'bus', and the previous run called it during warmup — so every 'ground level' shot came back as a view from the bus. While the player is in the bus state their position is bus-driven, so posing them was ignored too. Keep asking until the state changes, then land.

commits.subject: Pose the player, not the camera — the harness was measuring itself
commits.lede: Third design of this function and the first correct one.

commits.subject: The terrain was never white — it was never drawn
commits.lede: The white sheet was the ocean plane showing through where the island should have been. Terrain culled itself: frustumCulled was off and refreshLod decided visibility from a frustum built in lateUpdate out of ctx.camera. The capture harness re-poses the camera in renderOverride, which runs after lateUpdate, so every chunk answered against a camera pointing somewhere else and all 121 hid themselves.

commits.subject: Give the capture room to render the full shader path
commits.lede: Playwright's 30s screenshot default is not enough: compositing a 1600x900 frame of a 3 km island through a software rasteriser on the non-cheap path takes minutes, and the timeout threw away the entire run.

commits.subject: Force the shipped quality tier when capturing
commits.lede: detectQuality reads deviceMemory and core count, and this container has no GPU, so every capture so far ran at medium — which takes terrain's cheap shader path. Every frame I have reviewed was the low-end renderer, not the one a visitor with a real GPU gets. A capture that misrepresents the shipped experience is worse than no capture: it sends you fixing the wrong thing.

commits.subject: Add dz-probe: ask the running world about its own materials
commits.lede: A screenshot tells you a surface is wrong. It does not tell you whether the albedo map is missing, black, or merely unlit — and the terrain is currently rendering pure white while every other surface in the frame is correct, which is what a null map on a standard material looks like.

commits.subject: Visual fix pass: vegetation, colour grade, motion blur, storm wall
commits.lede: Four bugs, four real root causes.

commits.subject: Post-processing: continued fix-pass edits
commits.lede: Checkpoint while the visual fix agents are still writing.

commits.subject: Post-processing: motion blur and colour grade pass
commits.lede: Work in progress from the visual fix pass — the frame compiles clean and the remaining three fixes are still landing.

commits.subject: Fix the water shader's reserved word, and land the player before shooting
commits.lede: 'patch' is reserved in GLSL ES, so the whole water fragment shader failed to compile and the ocean never rendered its reflection path.

commits.subject: Stop tracking capture output
commits.lede: shots/ is scratch from dz-shot.mjs — five megabytes of PNG per run that a git add -A swept in. The world's card art is a deliberate, separate act.

commits.subject: Pose the shot camera in renderOverride, where it survives
commits.lede: Setting camera.position from outside does nothing: the player system owns the camera and rewrites it in lateUpdate, after any value the harness can poke in. The first run produced three byte-identical screenshots of the battle bus for exactly that reason. renderOverride is called last, so a pose installed there lands after the rig has had its say.

commits.subject: Close the two contract gaps the system authors worked around
commits.lede: RayHit now carries the collider's owner straight through. piece and target are the two owners collision recognises; everything else had no way home. Vegetation needs it to tell which tree a pickaxe just felled — without it a harvested trunk leaves its canopy standing in the air.

commits.subject: 📸 Gallery photography pass: four worlds get honest card art
commits.lede: The cards were selling the worlds short, and one was lying outright: the Moon card was islandArt — the moon has never once been the moon. Reshot in-engine off the clean canvas (no DOM chrome, which is what made the old captures look like screenshots of a UI instead of photographs of a place), each framed like a postcard:

commits.subject: Fix envHandle type so the environment probe's texture is reachable
commits.lede: buildEnvironment returns {texture, dispose} but the handle was declared as {dispose} only, so the assignment that feeds scene.environment did not typecheck. Without it every metal and glass surface renders flat grey.

commits.subject: Every spike is a real spike
commits.lede: Painted spikes are gone from this level entirely. They were the whole mechanic — rows drawn pixel-for-pixel like the lethal ones and harmless — and removing them means this stops being a tribute to the original's idea and becomes a straight Geometry Dash level. That is the call the owner made, and made clearly. It is done in full rather than halfway.

commits.subject: Nothing is spawned. It is drawn.
commits.lede: There is no random number generator left in this game, anywhere, and getting there took three attempts at the same problem.

commits.subject: Start on the Space Needle, and blow up when you hit it
commits.lede: Two things, and they turned out to be the same thing: the world needed something solid in it.

commits.subject: Fix a typecheck error in the space game's impact test
commits.lede: `harness`'s parameter type was inferred from its default argument, which is a planet — and a planet is the only body kind with a `planet` field, so every station and craft passed to it was a type error. `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json` has been failing on this; a broken typecheck on main hides everyone else's errors too.

commits.subject: Home Alone: infinite bricks
commits.lede: The roof of the brownstone from Lost in New York, imported wholesale into Winnetka. Space, or the 🧱 pad on a phone. It earns its place because it is the one thing in either film that is pure uncomplicated wish fulfilment: no setup, no clock, no plan — a boy with a brick and a man who deserves it.

commits.subject: Nothing floats but the gears
commits.lede: CLEANED UP. Decoy geometry now has to be standing on something. Spikes stand on the floor or on a plinth that reaches the floor; hanging rows hang from a ceiling that exists, or from a girder put there for exactly that purpose. A spike in mid-air is not something a level contains, and a screen of them reads as a rendering bug rather than as a lie. The one exception is the sawblade, because a sawblade hanging in mid-a

commits.subject: Home Alone: nobody is made of boxes any more
commits.lede: Limbs are tapered cylinders with a ball at every joint. This is the single biggest step from "assembled out of blocks" to "a person" — a forearm 15% narrower at the wrist than at the elbow reads as anatomy at a glance, where two boxes of equal width read as furniture however good the texture on them is. commits.subject: On a desktop, the cursor is the stick
commits.lede: Nobody could work out how to fly it. Two things were wrong.

commits.subject: Home Alone: the controls were lying about which way is forward
commits.lede: Both axes of the movement basis were negated. Pushing the stick forward walked him *at* the camera and pushing right strafed him left, which on a thumb reads as "sometimes it goes backwards" — and the playtest passed it for weeks because it only ever checked that he moved at all. A magnitude test cannot see a sign error. Six new checks can, and the basis is now written out in the comment so the next person does not h

commits.subject: One way home, in the same corner of every world
commits.lede: Thirty worlds, each its own engine, and the only thing they all agreed on was that there was no way out of them. Fullscreen worlds hide the global nav on purpose — it would sit on a crosshair — so the exit was whatever that world's author happened to build, if anything. On a phone there is no address bar to retype into, so several of them were a dead end.

commits.subject: A score written for the level, and checkpoints where they belong
commits.lede: CHECKPOINTS MOVE TO PRACTICE MODE, which is where Geometry Dash puts them and where they belong: a normal attempt is the whole level or nothing. The toggle is now PRACTICE rather than PURIST and it defaults off, so the default experience is the original bargain.
